Exports for the status metrics

The objection: "Status is a briefing chart." Why bother: the chart stays; the numbers on it stop being typed. Every number comes from the work itself, the same way every week, so the briefing becomes a discussion of what the numbers mean rather than an argument about whether they are right.

The A to Z status metrics (STATUS-METRICS.html) read the model repository and a folder of exports. gitlab.pl export DIR writes the exports from what GitLab knows; the weekly scheduled pipeline runs it, and it works the same against the offline emulator.

perl $KIT/bin/gitlab.pl --url https://gitlab.example.com --token-env STATUS_TOKEN --project tidewater/model \
     export exports --since 2026-10-05
perl $KIT/bin/status-metrics.pl collect --config metrics.json --history exports/history.jsonl
FileColumnsFeeds
ci_jobs.csvts, job, branch, result, minutespipeline health; time to restore a red develop (W); docs regeneration time (K)
mrs.csviid, title, author, source, target, created_at, merged_at, lead_hours, labels, stateMR lead time (N), who merges (Z)
issues.csviid, type, title, labels, milestone, assignee, state, created_at, closed_atsprint content, carryover, DR closure
defects.csvid, type, phase, found, closedinterface mismatches caught before integration (H)
tracker/sprint-N.csvthe stories of sprint N with status, blocked_days, blockersprint completion (X), blocked days and top blocker (Y)

The token needs only read_api. Make it a project access token, store it as a masked, protected CI/CD variable, and give it an expiry date (see below).

Administration

The objection: "IT runs the servers." Why bother: IT runs GitLab; the project's own upkeep (who has access, which tokens exist, whether the runner works) is configuration management, and it is a few minutes a week when kept up and a crisis when not.

Tom (configuration management) and Jim (owner) keep the project running. The wiki page Administration is the checklist; here is the reasoning.

Runners

A runner executes the jobs. The pipeline needs Perl, Git and a POSIX shell, and nothing else, so the simplest runner is a Windows shell runner using Git Bash: the same Perl the team uses on their laptops, so "passes on my machine" and "passes in CI" mean the same thing.

  1. On the runner machine: install Git for Windows; clone the kit (for example to C:\agile); download gitlab-runner.exe (the approved build) to C:\GitLab-Runner.
  2. In GitLab: Settings > CI/CD > Runners > New project runner, tags windows, perl. Copy the runner authentication token (it starts glrt-); it is shown once.
  3. Register and install it as a service, from an administrator prompt: 
    cd C:\GitLab-Runner
.\gitlab-runner.exe register --non-interactive --url https://gitlab.example.com --token %RUNNER_TOKEN% ^
    --executor shell --shell bash --description tidewater-win
.\gitlab-runner.exe install
.\gitlab-runner.exe start
  4. In config.toml, under the runner, add environment = ["KIT=/c/agile"], or set KIT as a CI/CD variable (the project file does).
  5. Keep the kit current on the runner: git -C C:\agile pull weekly, or pin it to a tag and update the pin by MR.

Tokens

  • Use project access tokens for automation (the weekly export), never a person's token: they stay valid when people leave, and they show up as a bot in the audit log.
  • Give each token the smallest scope (read_api for exports, api only for setup) and an expiry date. Rotate before expiry: Settings > Access tokens > Rotate, then update the CI/CD variable.
  • Store tokens in masked, protected CI/CD variables or in an environment variable on your machine (--token-env). Never on the command line (shell history) and never in a file in the repo: the secrets job and GitLab's secret detection look for glpat- tokens.

Backups

  • The instance: the GitLab administrator's daily gitlab-backup create, plus the configuration and secrets files kept apart from it.
  • The project, at each baseline: Settings > General > Advanced > Export project (repository, wiki, issues, MRs, labels, milestones), stored with the baseline's release evidence.
  • The repository and the wiki are Git: a git clone --mirror of each, kept on approved storage, is a complete copy of the model's history.

Members: on- and offboarding

  • Add people at the lowest role that lets them work: developer for engineers, maintainer only for those who cut baselines and manage the vendor branch. Set an access expiration date for temporary members.
  • On departure, the same day: remove the member from the group and project, revoke their tokens, rotate any shared variable they could read, reassign their issues and MRs, and update CODEOWNERS.
  • Review the member list each quarter (Manage > Members, sorted by last activity).

Audit and upgrades

  • Audit events (Secure > Audit events, Premium) record changes to protections, members, tokens and approvals. Review them monthly and after every change to project.conf.
  • Before a GitLab upgrade, read the release notes for removed CI keywords and API changes, then run gitlab.pl ci --list and gitlab.pl --dry-run setup against the new version.
  • Compare the server with the project file monthly: gitlab.pl --dry-run setup project.conf prints only what differs.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
remote: GitLab: You are not allowed to push code to protected branchesA direct push to develop or mainPush a feature branch and open an MR (flow start feature)
The first push to a new project is refusedmain was protected before it existedPush the skeleton first, then setup (the order)
Two pipelines for every push to an MRNo workflow:rulesKeep the workflow block of the template
Every job fails with KIT is not setThe CI/CD variable is missing or protected and the branch is notSet KIT unprotected, or on the runner's environment
lint is not 0/0A name does not resolve, or a warning was leftRun model.pl lint locally; the line numbers are Vim quickfix format
docs/ is staleThe model changed and the docs were not regeneratedmodel.pl docs, commit docs/
The MR cannot merge: "code owner approval required"A path's owner has not approvedAsk the owner shown on the file; changing CODEOWNERS in the same MR does not help (it is read from the target)
The issue did not close when the MR mergedThe MR merged into a branch that is not the defaultMake develop the default branch, or close it with /close
A drop merge conflicts in many filesSomeone edited vendor/prime, or reformatted converted files on developNever edit the vendor branch; edit converted files only where a TODO or tag requires it
The baseline job fails on a tagDocs not regenerated before the release merge, or a different kit versionFix on a hotfix/ branch and tag baseline-N.1; never move the tag
gitlab.pl: 401 UnauthorizedThe token expired, or lacks the scopeRotate it; api for setup, read_api for export
Labels like workflow::ready do not replace each otherScoped labels are PremiumOn Free remove the old label yourself (/unlabel), or move the card on the board

Glossary

The same glossary is the wiki page Glossary (tools/gitlab/templates/wiki/Glossary.md), so the team has it where they work.

You already know how to control a configuration. You have run CCBs, audited baselines, tracked action items and delivered CDRLs for decades. GitLab does the same jobs with different words, and it does many of them automatically. This page translates. Read the first table once; come back to the second when a word stops you.

One clash to watch: in configuration management a CI is a configuration item. In GitLab, CI means continuous integration, the automatic checks. This wiki writes "configuration item" in full and uses "CI" only for the checks.

What you already do, and what GitLab calls it

Systems engineering / CM termGitLab or DevSecOps termWhat is the sameWhat is different
Configuration itema folder or file under model/ (one per model package)it is under change control; it has an ownerthere are many small ones, and each change is recorded line by line
Master copy, controlled documentthe develop branchthe one copy everybody works fromnobody edits it directly; changes arrive only through merge requests
Released baselinea protected tag baseline-N on main, plus a release with notesfrozen; cited by analyses and reviewsthe server will not let anyone move or delete it, and the pipeline proves it rebuilds
Engineering Change Proposal (ECP), change request (CR)merge request (MR)proposes a change, shows exactly what changes, is reviewed and approvedsmall (days, not months), and the exact lines changed are shown side by side
Configuration Control Board (CCB) approvalapproval on the MR, by the code owners of the changed partsthe right authority says yes before it goes inper change, on line; nobody waits for the monthly board
Redlines, markupsreview comments on lines of the MR, and suggestionscomments pinned to the textthe author applies a suggestion with one click
Configuration audit (FCA/PCA)the pipeline: automatic checks on every changechecks the configuration against its rulesruns in minutes on every change, not once at the end
Configuration status accountingthe Git history, the merge log, gitlab.pl exportwho changed what, when, under which changecomplete and exact, with no one typing it up
Revision (Rev A, Rev B)commitone recorded change with an author and a datethere are many, each small; the commit id is the revision number
Revision history blockgit log, CHANGELOG.mdthe list of changesgenerated from the work itself
Working draftbranch (a feature/... branch)your copy while you workit lives days, and Git brings your changes back in
Incorporating an approved changemergethe change becomes part of the master copyGit applies it line by line; it stops only where two changes touch the same lines (a merge conflict)
CDRL delivery from the primea prime drop committed on the vendor branch vendor/primethe contractor's deliverable, received and checkedit is converted and merged into our model, keeping our own edits
Discrepancy / deficiency reportan issue with the label type::discrepancya written finding against a deliverabletracked on a board until the drop that fixes it closes it
Action itemissue (a task or story)owner, due date, statusvisible to all, linked to the change that closes it
Action item tracker (spreadsheet)issue boardone row per action, a status columnthe status is a label, the board updates itself
WBS elementepic and tome labelsgroups work into a hierarchysized by time: an epic fits in a semester, a tome in a year
IMS milestone, eventa release / baselinea dated program event—
A two-week period of workmilestone Sprint Na time box with a list of workGitLab calls any dated time box a milestone; ours are sprints, not IMS events
Data Item Description (DID), document templateissue template, merge request templatesays what goes in each sectionfilled in on line; GitLab offers it when you create the item
Systems Engineering Plan, process documentsthe wikihow we workshort pages, versioned, changed like the model
Requirements traceability matrix (RTM)the trace job and docs/Traceability.mdwhich requirement is satisfied and verified by whatrebuilt on every change from the model itself
Verification cross-reference matrix (VCRM)verify relationships in model/requirements/Verification.sysml + results in verification/*.csv, the vcrm jobwhich case verifies which requirement, and its newest verdictbuilt by the pipeline on every change, published on the Pages site
Peer review, desk checkMR reviewa second engineer reads the changethe change is small, so the review takes minutes
Signature block, sign-off dateapproval, merged atwho approved, and whenrecorded by the server, cannot be backdated
Distribution list@mentions, notificationswho is toldpeople are told about what concerns them, as it happens
Weekly status chartthe status metrics from gitlab.pl exportprogress and problems for the programcomputed from the work, not typed up on Thursday night

GitLab and DevSecOps words

WordMeaning here
DevSecOpsDevelopment, security and operations done together, in small changes, with automated checks. For us: every model change is small, reviewed, checked by machine and recorded, and security checks run on every change rather than at the end.
Repository (repo)The folder of files under version control, with its full history. Ours is tidewater/model.
GitThe version-control program. It records every change to every file.
CloneYour own full copy of the repository on your laptop.
CommitOne recorded change: what changed, who, when, and a message saying why.
Push / pullSend your commits to the server / bring others' commits to your laptop.
BranchA line of work. develop is the master copy; you work on your own branch and merge it back.
Default branchThe branch GitLab shows first and closes issues on: develop.
MergeBring the changes of one branch into another.
Merge conflictGit cannot merge on its own because both sides changed the same lines. A person picks the right text.
Merge request (MR)A request to merge your branch into develop, with the changes shown, a discussion, checks and approvals. Our ECP.
ApprovalA reviewer's "yes" on an MR.
Code ownerThe person who must approve changes to a given folder, listed in the file CODEOWNERS.
Protected branchA branch nobody can change directly; only an approved MR can. main and develop are protected.
TagA permanent name for one exact state of the repository. baseline-1 is a tag.
Protected tagA tag nobody can move or delete.
ReleaseA tag plus release notes, shown on GitLab's Releases page.
GitflowThe branch scheme we use: main for baselines, develop for integration, short branches for each change.
Feature branchA short-lived branch for one task: feature/19-stations-level-tags.
Release branchA branch for preparing a baseline: release/baseline-1.
HotfixA small, urgent fix to a released baseline, on a hotfix/... branch.
Back-mergeMerging main into develop after a release or hotfix, so nothing is lost.
Vendor branchvendor/prime: exactly what the converters make of each prime drop, never edited by hand.
Prime dropOne delivery of the prime's v1 model and DOORS data (XMI, ReqIF, CSV, MANIFEST).
PipelineThe automatic checks GitLab runs on every change: our configuration audit.
JobOne check in the pipeline, such as lint or trace.
StageA group of jobs that run together; stages run in order.
RunnerThe machine that runs the jobs.
CI/CDContinuous integration / continuous delivery: checking and delivering every change automatically.
.gitlab-ci.ymlThe file that defines the pipeline, written in YAML.
YAMLA plain-text format for settings, with indentation for structure.
ArtifactA file a job keeps after it runs (a report, a count).
LintAn automatic check of a model's structure: names resolve, nothing dangles.
Grammar checkAn automatic check that each file is valid SysML v2 text.
Secrets scanAn automatic check that no password, token or key was committed.
TokenA password for a program (a script, the pipeline) instead of a person.
IssueA work item: an action item, a story, a task, a defect, a discrepancy report.
LabelA tag on an issue or MR that says what kind it is, where it belongs, or its status.
Scoped labelA label written key::value; an item has only one value per key (Premium).
MilestoneA dated time box in GitLab. Ours are the sprints.
BoardIssues shown as cards in columns, one column per status label.
Quick actionA command in a comment, such as /label ~"workflow::done" or /close.
MarkdownThe plain-text formatting GitLab uses in every text field: bold, - [ ] checklist, tables with ``.
WikiThe project's pages of procedures and decisions.
SprintTwo weeks of work with a goal, planned at the start and reviewed at the end.
TaskWork of less than a week (5 points or fewer; one point is one ideal day).
StorySeveral tasks that deliver something useful within one sprint.
EpicSeveral stories finished within a semester (13 sprints).
TomeSeveral epics finished within a year.
ProjectThe whole effort, years long: here, the port and its maintenance.
PointThe size of a task, in ideal person-days.
Stand-upA 15-minute daily meeting: what I did yesterday, what I do today, what blocks me.
Definition of DoneThe checklist a task or story must meet before it counts as done.
Definition of ReadyThe checklist a story must meet before a sprint takes it.
SysML v2 textThe model written as text files, readable and comparable line by line, instead of a Cameo project.
TODO lineA line the converter writes for something it could not translate; a person closes it.
DeltaWhat changed in the prime's v1 model between two drops.
DriftA requirement whose text differs between DOORS and the model.
Orphan requirementA requirement nothing satisfies.
Unverified requirementA requirement no verification case verifies.
EmulatorThe kit's offline stand-in for a GitLab server, for practice and testing.
Free / PremiumGitLab's product tiers. A few features (enforced code-owner approval, epics, iterations, scoped labels) need Premium; this wiki says which, and what to do on Free.

Command reference

bin/gitlab.pl talks to a GitLab server through its REST API (with curl, which Git for Windows ships) or to the offline emulator, with the same commands. perl bin/gitlab.pl help COMMAND prints the details.

gitlab.pl [--url URL [--token-env VAR] | --local DIR] [--project PATH] [--as USER] [--now ISO] [--dry-run] COMMAND
  setup FILE                         apply a project file (settings, members, protections, labels, milestones, rules, variables)
  sprints START COUNT [--weeks 2] [--prefix "Sprint "]
  issue new TITLE [--template F] [--label L]... [--milestone M] [--assign U] [--type task|issue|incident]
  issue list [--state opened|closed|all] [--label L] | show IID | close IID | note IID TEXT|--file F | link IID TARGET
  mr new --source B [--target B] --title T [--template F] [--label L]... | list | show IID | approve IID | merge IID | note IID TEXT
  pipeline run REF [--source push|web|schedule] | list | show ID
  tag NAME REF [--message M] | release TAG [--notes FILE] [--name N]
  wiki put TITLE FILE | wiki list
  export DIR [--since DATE] [--until DATE]
  ci [--file .gitlab-ci.yml] [--event push|merge_request_event|tag|schedule|web] [--branch B] [--target B]
     [--tag T] [--var K=V]... [--job NAME] [--manual] [--list]
  flow init | flow start feature|release|hotfix NAME | flow publish | flow finish [--title T] [--template F]
     | flow vendor DROPDIR VERSION | flow sync
  help [COMMAND]
